newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Standa denies layoff plans.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Standa denies layoff plans.

text.p: Italy's Standa SpA group, the country's second largest retailing chain, denied trade union claims it planned to cut 1,000 jobs.

Employees at the group, owned by Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest SpA, staged strikes throughout Italy on Thursday after union leaders claimed Standa planned to lay off some 1,000 of its 12,000 employees.
The unions said Standa had already started procedures to cut some 150 jobs in Milan and charged that the group's planned 900 billion lire investment and relaunch plan was insufficient.

"Standa does not intend to cut 1,000 jobs and denies that it has set in motion any dismissal procedures at its Milan headquarters," the group said in a statement, adding that the clarification was necessary after the union claims.

"It is absurd to judge an investment plan of over 900 billion lire insufficient," it said, adding that in 1996 it had launched a new type of large store, expanded in the food sector, had bought the majority of a specialised toy chain Toys Center, and had more than doubled its Blockbuster home video stores.
Standa made a group net loss of 93.7 billion lire in 1996 after a 139.7 billion lire profit in 1995.

Its statement added that it had identified badly performing areas "where store management has turned out to be economically untenable. In such cases the group is working on accords with businessmen at national and regional level for the sale of the stores, while at the same time safeguarding job levels."
